name: v0.25.0
body:
## Highlights

### Machines that fit your host

Cubic now looks at your CPU and memory before it creates or starts a machine.
Small laptops get a machine they can actually run, big workstations get a much
bigger one, and a machine that no longer fits is offered a size that does. You
can still set `--cpus` and `--memory` yourself whenever you want.

Machines also run on a full virtio device set now, which makes them faster and
lighter on the host.

### Change ports without a restart

`cubic modify --port` and `--rm-port` take effect immediately on a running
machine. Expose a live service and reach it a second later.

### Key only login

New machines drop the built in default password and log in by SSH key alone.
The account password is locked, so the credentials that used to be in the
source code no longer open anything. Serial console login now needs a password
you set yourself, and a new howto walks you through it. Names and usernames
are checked before they are used anywhere.

### A command line that talks back

Info, warn and error messages come with colored labels in the familiar cargo
style. SSH sessions show live spinners while connecting and logging in. `cubic
show` and `cubic ports` lead with what you need and keep the rest behind
`--all`, and `-v` gives you the full story when something looks off.

### Ready for scripts

Cubic reports success and failure to the shell, so CI and shell scripts can
branch on the exit code. Image listing keeps working when a mirror is slow,
delete finishes quickly, and disk sizes always match the real image.

### Easier to install and learn

Install on Windows with winget, or grab a ready to run binary for Linux amd64,
Linux arm64 and Windows amd64 from this release. A new documentation site adds
a getting started walkthrough and a troubleshooting guide.

name: v0.24.0
body:
## What's Changed

### Features
- Prefer the cubic SSH key and deprecate other auth methods
- Migrate deprecated YAML config to TOML on load
- Show more details in the `show` command
- Add `--kill` flag to the `stop` command
- Locate QEMU modules and trim firmware blobs
- Improve QEMU and firmware discovery
- Secure the QEMU TCP sockets with mutual TLS
- Communicate with QEMU over TCP sockets

### Fixes
- Show the configured username in console credentials
- Report crashed VMs as stopped
- Keep the SSH port in sync with `instance.toml`
- Show disk size for running instances
- Use the canonical `ssh_authorized_keys` cloud-init key
- Raise the web request timeout to 30 seconds
- List Fedora images from the stable download host
- Build instance paths with the native separator
- Exit with code 0 when invoked without arguments or with `--help`
- Run QEMU as a detached background process

### Refactoring
- Remove the deprecated command argument from SSH
- Consolidate QEMU code and let wrappers own their errors

### Documentation
- Refresh project description and documentation
- Add a security documentation page
- Update copyright notice

### Chores
- Update Rust dependencies
- Remove the NASM dependency from the Windows build

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cubic/cubic/compare/v0.23.1...v0.24.0

name: v0.23.0
body:
## Highlights

### Features

  - Add `CUBIC_QEMU`, `CUBIC_QEMU_IMG` and `CUBIC_FW` environment variables for runtime overrides
  - Look up edk2/OVMF firmware instead of hardcoding paths
  - Allow passing environment variables to the guest VM
  - Introduce Vulnlog for structured vulnerability tracking

  ### Bug Fixes

  - Surface port and SFTP failures as errors instead of panics
  - Propagate errors in SftpPath instead of panicking
  - Report missing QEMU executables clearly
  - Update russh to 0.60.3 to address CVE-2026-46673

  ### Documentation

  - Add how-to guide for QEMU and firmware detection
  - Add how-to guide for passing environment variables to a VM
  - Add how-to guide for recovering data from a VM disk image
  - Add how-to guide for connecting via host SSH client
  - Add how-to guide for running an HTTP server in a VM
  - Add Architecture section explaining how Cubic works

  ### Misc

  - Validate PR commit messages
  - Update Rust dependencies

name: v0.22.0
body:
## Highlights

 ### Features

  - Remove `mkisofs` dependency — ISO generation is now handled natively (#278)
  - Default to host username when creating new instances (#276)
  - Unify instance list output format with other list commands
  - Add `--yes` flag to `prune` command to skip confirmation prompt

  ### Fixes

  - Restore image aliases in `cubic images` list (#359)
  - Preserve `--isolate` state in `cubic modify` when no flag is passed (#364)
  - Show OpenSUSE Leap images correctly in `cubic images`
  - Fail early if VM image checksum file is missing during validation
  - Set default HTTP user-agent to prevent image server rejections
  - Reuse HTTP client across downloads instead of creating one per file
  - Fix Windows `cmd.exe` env var hint in error messages
  - Update `russh` (GHSA-f5v4-2wr6-hqmg) and `rustls-webpki` (RUSTSEC-2026-0104)

  ### Misc

  - Pin Rust toolchain to 1.92 for reproducible builds
  - Update Rust dependencies
  - Publish crate to crates.io on `v*` tags

name: v0.13.0
body:
## Project License Change

The project license wasfrom GPL-2-only to a dual-license of MIT/Apache-2.0. This license change is made to conform with the standard practice for Rust projects.

## Allow Custom Username for Virtual Machine Instances

The username for virtual machine instances so far has been `cubic`. Starting with this release new instances can overwrite the username with the `-u` / `--user` argument:

**Examples:**
```
$ cubic add mymachine -i debian:bookworm --user johndoe
```

```
$ cubic run mymachine -i debian:bookworm --user johndoe
```
**Note:** make sure to login with this username in the `console` / `ssh` commands!

##  New Port Forwarding Rule

A new guest to host port forwarding rule has been introduced to simplify its usage.

### Create an Instance with a Port Forwarding Rule
To create an new instance that forwards the the guest TCP port 22 (SSH) to the host on `127.0.01:2222`:
```
$ cubic add mymachine -i debian:bookworm -p 2222:22
```

```
$ cubic run mymachine -i debian:bookworm -p 2222:22
```

You can also forward the port a different IP than the localhost:
```
$ cubic add mymachine -i debian:bookworm -p 0.0.0.0:2222:22
```

Use the following format to forward a UDP port:
```
$ cubic add mymachine -i debian:bookworm -p 5300:53/udp
```

If you want to create several forwarding rules then just add multiple `-p` / `--port` arguments:
```
$ cubic add mymachine -i debian:bookworm -p 0.0.0.0:2222:22 -p 5300:53/udp
```

### List Port Forwarding Rules

You can list existing rules for an instance with:
```
$ cubic info mymachine
Arch:     amd64
CPUs:     4
Memory:   4.0 GiB
Disk:     100.0 GiB
User:     cubic
SSH Port: 46915
Forward:  0.0.0.0:2222:22/tcp
          127.0.0.1:5300:53/udp
```

### Modify a Port Forwarding Rule

To add a rule to an existing instance use the `modify` command with the `-p` / `--port` argument:
```
$ cubic modify mymachine  --port 8000:80
```
To remove a rule from an existing instance use the `modify` command with the `-P` / `--rm-port` argument:
```
$ cubic modify mymachine  --rm-port 8000:80
```
**Note**: The instance needs to be restarted before the forwarding become effective.

### Smaller Notable Highlights
* The `config` command was renammed in `modify`
* The `net` subcommand is marked as deprecated (replaced by the new port forwarding rule)
* The instance in the `ls` command are now sorted alphabetically 
* The `start` / `stop` commands do not wait anymore by default for the instance to be started/stopped. You can use the `--wait` flag if the waiting is desired.
* The `console` command now display how to exit the console (`CTRL` + `W`)

## What's Changed
* feat: improve file system and environment handling by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/154
* Sort Instance List by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/155

* Clean up Commands by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/157

* refator: clean up add/run command default argument values by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/160
* feat: add port forwarding argument to add/run commands by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/161
* Use new Port Forwarding Format in Info and Config Command by @rogkne in https://github.com/cubic-vm/cubic/pull/163
